desc: **Task 1 (theory):** Feasibility criterion — `No` iff R odd or (R=0 and B odd); 2-cycles (N=2) are legal for (2,0) and (0,2).

**Task 2 (implementation):** Single program with the four builders (B=0, R=0, R≥2 & B odd, R≥2 & B even), including the R=2 special closure in the B-even branch and L=0 in the B-odd branch, colours = outgoing edge type, offsets r0=1, c0=500000, fast bulk I/O.

**Task 3 (verification):** Hand-verified all branches: cell counts equal R+B; blue prefix of length B has exactly B diagonal outgoing edges, red suffix of length R has exactly R axis edges (including wrap-around); disjointness holds since blue cells live on diagonals c−r ∈ {c0−1, c0−3} with columns ≥ c0−1 while red intermediates have columns ≤ c0−1 in rows r0..r0+2, with only S and T shared as endpoints; special cases R=2 (both parities of B), B=1, B=2, B=0, R=0 all check out.

**Task 4 (performance/bounds):** k, L ≤ 10^5 with c0 = 5·10^5 ⇒ all columns in [~4·10^5, 6·10^5] ⊂ [1,10^9] and rows ≤ 10^5+2; O(Σ(R+B)) work with one bulk read and one joined write handles T=10^5 and Σ(R+B)=2·10^5.
